advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have the workspace probe echo an explicit `clean` / `dirty` / `error` token and report anything other than `clean` (including a docker exec failure) as an error or warning marker
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:706: state="$(docker exec "$name" sh -c 'd="$MCP_CODE_DIR"
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:708: [ -z "$(GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 git -C "$d" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null)" ] || echo dirty' \
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:709: 2>/dev/null)" || return 0
Inside the exec, a failing `git status` gives empty stdout with stderr suppressed. `[ -z "" ]` is then true, so 'dirty' is never echoed. A failing docker exec hits `|| return 0`.
advisory.finding: mcp_check_code_workspace fails open. If docker exec fails, git is missing, or `git status` errors (for example a corrupt index after an OOM kill), the probe produces no output and is treated as a clean workspace. It cannot tell 'checked and clean' apart from 'the check never ran'.
scenarios: After an OOM kill the index is corrupt, so `git status` exits non-zero and the tick reports nothing while gates read a stale tree.
docker exec fails (daemon hiccup, container is exiting) and nothing is reported.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the exec script, capture git status's exit code: `out=$(GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 git -C "$d" status --porcelain) || { echo error; exit 0; }; [ -z "$out" ] && echo clean || echo dirty`. On the host, treat any state other than `clean` (or the explicit no-checkout case) as a reportable error.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Run the code-workspace probe under the entrypoint's checkout lock (e.g. `mcp-entrypoint.sh --with-dir-lock`), or only report after the dirty state persists across two ticks
evidence: infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:231: with_dir_lock "$code_dir" "code checkout" refresh_code_locked
infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:276: if ! git -C "${MCP_CODE_DIR}" merge --ff-only origin/main; then
infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:294: git clone --filter=blob:none --single-branch --branch main \
infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:375: provision_store &
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:764: mcp_check_code_workspace
The probe never calls with_dir_lock / `--with-dir-lock`, so nothing stops it running concurrently with the refresh.
advisory.finding: The tick probe reads the workspace without taking the checkout lock that refresh_code_locked holds. A no-op tick that runs while a freshly restarted container's background refresh is mid `merge --ff-only` will see a partially updated tree and raise mcp-code-workspace-stuck for a healthy refresh. The checkout is a blobless clone, so the merge fetches blobs lazily during checkout, which can make this window long.
scenarios: restart:always brings the MCP container back after an OOM kill. Its background refresh fast-forwards many commits, the next timer tick lands mid-checkout, and AUTODEPLOY_ERROR pages.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Let recovery work from the existing local origin/main (best-effort fetch, then search the ancestry path), or report a fetch failure as `unreachable` rather than `dirty`
evidence: infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:248: git -C "$dir" fetch origin main || return 1
infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:264: if [ -n "$(git -C "${MCP_CODE_DIR}" status --porcelain)" ] &&
infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:265: ! recover_interrupted_fast_forward; then
infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:267: code_workspace_marker dirty
infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:270: if ! git -C "${MCP_CODE_DIR}" fetch origin main; then
advisory.finding: recover_interrupted_fast_forward runs a fresh `git fetch origin main` before trying recovery. When the remote is unreachable, the provably recoverable state is refused and logged with reason `dirty` instead of `unreachable`. Recovery does not need the network: the interrupted merge was toward the origin/main already stored locally, so the target commit is already reachable from the local origin/main ref.
scenarios: The container restarts during a GitHub or network outage after an interrupted fast-forward. Recovery is skipped, a `dirty` marker is emitted, and the tick pages as stuck, even though the workspace could have been fixed offline.
advisory.suggested_fix: Make the fetch best-effort (`git -C "$dir" fetch origin main || true`) and search `${old_head}..origin/main` using whatever origin/main is present locally. The later fetch in refresh_code_locked will still classify an unreachable remote correctly.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wire MCP_CODE_WORKSPACE_ERROR into a metric or alarm, or extend the tick probe to page when the live workspace is behind origin/main beyond a threshold
evidence: infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:234: # Emit one record-anchored marker line per refusal so the host journal can count it.
search_files for MCP_CODE_WORKSPACE_ERROR: the only hits are the entrypoint printf, the runbook and one test assertion. There is no metric filter or alarm.
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:708: [ -z "$(GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 git -C "$d" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null)" ] || echo dirty'
advisory.finding: Only the `dirty` refusal reaches a page. The `diverged` and `unreachable` refusals, which also leave gates pinned to a stale tree, only print an MCP_CODE_WORKSPACE_ERROR marker. Nothing in the repo consumes that marker, and the tick probe only checks `git status`.
scenarios: A stale `.git/index.lock` or local divergence makes `merge --ff-only` fail. A `diverged` marker is logged, the tree stays clean, the tick probe reports nothing, and gates read an old tree indefinitely.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Log the container name (`$2`) in the fake docker exec branch
evidence: tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py:118: echo "exec ${*: -3:1}" >> "$LOG"
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:706: docker exec "$name" sh -c '...' gives positional args exec, NAME, sh, -c, SCRIPT, so the third from last is `sh`.
advisory.finding: The fake docker `exec` branch logs `${*: -3:1}`. For `docker exec NAME sh -c SCRIPT` that is `sh`, not the container name, so the command log entry `exec sh` is misleading for anyone who later asserts on it.
scenarios: A future test asserts that `exec rebar-mcp-live-8092` appears in the command log and fails confusingly.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Take the `code checkout` dir lock (or skip the check while the entrypoint's refresh holds it) in mcp_check_code_workspace, so its `git status --porcelain` cannot see a mid-merge or pre-recovery tree as a stuck workspace
evidence: Shared resource: the git checkout at "$MCP_CODE_DIR" (index and working tree compared with HEAD), on a volume shared by blue-green and restarted containers: mcp-entrypoint.sh:208 "# Serialize blue-green and restart writers on the checkout inode."

Sibling accessor and its guard: mcp-entrypoint.sh:231 `with_dir_lock "$code_dir" "code checkout" refresh_code_locked`. Inside the lock it reads at mcp-entrypoint.sh:264 `git -C "${MCP_CODE_DIR}" status --porcelain` and writes at :254 `git -C "$dir" update-ref ... HEAD "$target" "$old_head"` and :276 `git -C "${MCP_CODE_DIR}" merge --ff-only origin/main`. The lock is an fcntl.flock: mcp-entrypoint.sh:106 `fcntl.flock(9, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)`.

Unlocked twin (new): autodeploy.sh:708-709 runs `docker exec "$name" sh -c '... GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 git -C "$d" status --porcelain ... || echo dirty'` with no with_dir_lock / `--with-dir-lock` seam, even though the entrypoint offers one (mcp-entrypoint.sh:364-367 `if [ "${1:-}" = "--with-dir-lock" ]; then ... with_dir_lock "$@"`).
Executor 1: the container entrypoint's background provisioning, mcp-entrypoint.sh:375 `provision_store &`, which calls provision_code -> refresh_code -> refresh_code_locked (merge / recovery).

Executor 2: the autodeploy no-op tick. autodeploy.sh:763 `mcp_self_heal_live_backend || exit 1` then autodeploy.sh:764 `mcp_check_code_workspace`. Self-heal can start the container at autodeploy.sh:685 `docker start "$name"` and returns after mcp_wait_health_contract (autodeploy.sh:689). Checkout provisioning is explicitly not gated on health: mcp-entrypoint.sh:184 "Container promotion never waits for this checkout".

Interleaving window: the probe's read `git status --porcelain` (autodeploy.sh:709) runs while the entrypoint writes the tree with `merge --ff-only` (mcp-entrypoint.sh:276). It can also land after an interrupted-fast-forward restart but before recovery moves the ref at mcp-entrypoint.sh:254. Both are states where status is non-empty but the entrypoint is not stuck.

Harm: the probe's non-empty status becomes a persisted `err mcp-code-workspace-stuck` (autodeploy.sh:711) whose text says the entrypoint 'refuses to refresh it, so gates read a stale tree'. That is false here, and the marker is counted into rebar/host:deploy_errors.

Mitigating context for scoring: the alarm needs 2 of 4 900s periods (infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:28-30, 'a single transient error still doesn't page'), and a self-heal tick already emits `err mcp-live-backend-down` (autodeploy.sh:679) in the same tick. So a single spurious marker mainly misattributes the cause and adds to the count. It pages only if it combines with another error in a second period, or if the refresh (blob fetches in the blobless clone) runs past a tick boundary.
advisory.finding: mcp_check_code_workspace reads the shared MCP code checkout's dirty state without the checkout lock that the entrypoint's own dirty-check, recovery and fast-forward hold. On a tick where self-heal has just restarted the live backend, the probe can catch the tree partway through `merge --ff-only`, or in the interrupted-fast-forward state that recover_interrupted_fast_forward is about to fix. It then emits a false `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR mcp-code-workspace-stuck` saying the entrypoint refuses to refresh.
scenarios: The container is OOM-killed mid-refresh (the very incident this fixes) while the live backend is not running. The next tick self-heals it with `docker start`, health passes, and mcp_check_code_workspace runs while the background refresh_code_locked is still in recover_interrupted_fast_forward's `fetch origin main` before update-ref. The probe sees the interrupted-ff dirty tree and reports mcp-code-workspace-stuck, even though recovery succeeds seconds later.

A restart (restart:always, or self-heal) triggers a refresh whose `merge --ff-only` is checking out files (lazy blob fetches in the blobless clone). A tick probing at that moment sees modified files and reports a stuck workspace.
advisory.suggested_fix: Run the probe under the entrypoint's existing lock seam, e.g. `docker exec "$name" /path/to/mcp-entrypoint.sh --with-dir-lock "$MCP_CODE_DIR" "code checkout" sh -c '<status check>'`. With a short MCP_RECLONE_LOCK_WAIT, treat a failure to get the lock as 'refresh in progress' and emit nothing. Alternatively, skip the check on a tick where self-heal just restarted the backend, or report only after the dirty state has persisted across two consecutive ticks.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that combines an interrupted fast-forward with an unstaged tracked-file edit and asserts returncode 1, HEAD unchanged and the edit preserved
evidence: infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:246: `git -C "$dir" diff --quiet || return 1`
infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:254-256: update-ref moves HEAD, and only after that does `[ -z "$(git -C "$dir" status --porcelain)" ] || return 1` run

The new tests cover the untracked case (tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py:525-539) and the staged-tree-not-on-main case (505-522). No test runs _interrupt_fast_forward followed by an unstaged edit to a tracked file.

Named violating input: _interrupt_fast_forward(checkout, _advance(source)); then (checkout / 'file.txt').write_text('edited\n') with no `git add`. With the guard removed, HEAD moves off stuck_head even though provisioning returns 1.
advisory.finding: No test covers the unstaged-modification guard (`git diff --quiet || return 1`) in recover_interrupted_fast_forward. If that line were deleted, the test suite would stay green: write-tree takes the index, which still matches the target commit, so update-ref moves HEAD under an unstaged edit. Only the final `status --porcelain` check would then refuse, after the ref has already moved.
scenarios: A later edit to the guard ordering, or its removal, lets the ref move under a modified working tree, and no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add test_unstaged_edit_blocks_recovery_of_an_interrupted_fast_forward, modeled on the untracked-file test: after _interrupt_fast_forward, write file.txt without staging it. Assert (result.returncode, _head(checkout), (checkout/'file.txt').read_text()) == (1, stuck_head, 'edited\n').

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the MCP_CODE_WORKSPACE_ERROR marker with reason "diverged" and with reason "unreachable" in the existing refusal-distinguishing test
evidence: infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:272: `code_workspace_marker unreachable`
infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:278: `code_workspace_marker diverged`
tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py:522 asserts only `'MCP_CODE_WORKSPACE_ERROR {"reason": "dirty"' in result.stderr`

tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py:420-424 (test_refusals_distinguish_dirty_diverged_and_unreachable) checks only the human-readable lines ('diverged code checkout', 'origin/main unreachable'), not the markers
Inputs: a diverged checkout (local commit, then _advance(source)), and an origin set to tmp_path/'missing.git'
advisory.finding: The newly added `code_workspace_marker unreachable` and `code_workspace_marker diverged` lines are never asserted. The commit says 'Any other refusal emits an MCP_CODE_WORKSPACE_ERROR marker', but only the dirty reason is checked. Removing either line, or giving it the wrong reason string, would not fail any test.
scenarios: The marker's format or reason drifts for diverged or unreachable workspaces, so the host journal stops counting those refusals without notice.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_refusals_distinguish_dirty_diverged_and_unreachable, also assert that '"reason": "dirty"' is in dirty_result.stderr, '"reason": "diverged"' is in diverged_result.stderr and '"reason": "unreachable"' is in unreachable_result.stderr.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the fake `docker exec` run its trailing `sh -c` script with MCP_CODE_DIR pointed at a temp git repo, or test the probe script directly against clean and dirty repos
evidence: tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py:116-120: `exec) ... [ -f "$DS/code-workspace-dirty" ] && echo dirty; exit 0 ;;` (the sh -c script argument is never run)

infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh (added): `state="$(docker exec "$name" sh -c 'd="$MCP_CODE_DIR"\n [ -n "$d" ] && [ -e "$d/.git" ] || exit 0\n [ -z "$(GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 git -C "$d" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null)" ] || echo dirty' 2>/dev/null)" || return 0`

Named input: a probe script whose dirtiness test were inverted, or whose `$MCP_CODE_DIR` were quoted so it expands on the host instead of in the container, still passes test_no_op_tick_reports_a_stuck_mcp_code_workspace unchanged.
blocking.finding: The autodeploy test's fake `docker exec` ignores the probe script it receives and prints `dirty` whenever a seeded file exists. No test ever runs the newly added in-container shell probe: the empty-MCP_CODE_DIR exit, the missing-.git exit and the `git status --porcelain` dirtiness check. The test only checks that autodeploy turns the literal string `dirty` into an err marker.
scenarios: A probe-script bug, such as wrong quoting or a condition that always reports clean, means a stuck production workspace never pages, while CI stays green.
blocking.suggested_fix: In the stub, have `exec` shift past the container name and run the remaining argv (`sh -c <script>`) with MCP_CODE_DIR set to a fixture repo. In the dirty case, make the fixture repo dirty instead of seeding a marker file. Also cover an unset MCP_CODE_DIR, which should emit no marker.
